findings.title: Zod SafeParse wrapper object is stored as the credential key, corrupting Google credentials on every refresh
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse result object ({ success: true, data: {...} }), but line 97-100 stores that whole wrapper as the credential key: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...); await prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Before this PR the key was the plain parsed token object. After the first access-token refresh, credential.key in the DB becomes {"success":true,"data":{...tokens...}}, and the next time GoogleCalendarService is constructed `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws because the tokens are nested under `data`. This breaks Google Calendar for every user whose token refreshes, on default (non-sync) installs too. Extract `.data` (or change the helper to return parsed data) before persisting.

findings.title: Sync-mode returns a raw fetch Response but several callers expect parsed/library-specific shapes
findings.body: In sync mode this helper returns the unparsed fetch Response, but multiple integrations handle the return value as if it were the library-specific response: googlecalendar reads `res?.data` (a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws a TypeError that is swallowed by the catch and the expired token is silently reused); hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts treats it as HubspotToken (`expiresIn` is undefined so expiryDate becomes NaN, `setAccessToken(undefined)` is called, and the Response object itself is persisted as the credential key); zohocrm and zoho-bigin read `tokenInfo.data.error`, throwing TypeError since `.data` is undefined. Credential sync mode is therefore broken (or corrupts stored credentials) for google-calendar, hubspot, zohocrm and zoho-bigin. The helper should parse the JSON body and normalize the response shape, or callers must be adapted.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is not valid zod: it strips everything except access_token and forces refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` do not create a catch-all (they evaluate to a fixed string such as "[object Object]"), and z.object strips unknown keys by default. So in sync mode the parse result contains only `access_token`; any expiry field returned by the sync endpoint is dropped, and lines 25-27 then set `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token". Consequences downstream: office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts line 264 spreads this over the stored credentials, overwriting the user's real refresh token with "refresh_token" in the DB; zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000` where expires_in was stripped, storing NaN and also persisting the placeholder refresh token. Use z.catchall/passthrough for the permissive schema and preserve real expiry/refresh-token data.

findings.title: Credential primary key passed as Cal.com userId to the credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId, which is POSTed to the self-hoster's sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. Bigin passes `credentialId` (credential.id) instead of the user's id. The sync endpoint will look up a user whose id equals the credential id and either fail or return another user's tokens, which then get stored under this credential. Pass credential.userId (the method currently only receives credentialId and credentialKey, so it needs the credential object or userId).

findings.title: New code uses prisma without importing it, breaking the build
findings.body: The newly added token-refresh block calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)` but the file's imports (lines 1-20) contain no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. TypeScript compilation/type-check fails with "Cannot find name 'prisma'", so the package no longer builds.

findings.title: appStoreMetadata is looked up by DB slug, but it is keyed by app directory name — sync 404s for most apps
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app folder names (e.g. "googlecalendar", "office365calendar", "office365video", "zoomvideo", "larkcalendar"), while `app.slug` from the App table uses the public slugs used everywhere else in this PR ("google-calendar", "office365-calendar", "msteams", "zoom", "lark-calendar"). `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]` is therefore undefined for those apps and the webhook returns 404 "App not found" — credential sync only works for the few apps whose slug equals the directory name (hubspot, zohocrm, salesforce, zoho-bigin). Look metadata up by each entry's own `slug` property or maintain a slug→metadata map.

findings.title: Refresh runs on every service construction and the fresh token is then ignored
findings.body: getClient (invoked from the constructor) now performs an unconditional refresh-token grant against Salesforce every time the service is instantiated — adding a blocking HTTP call and token churn to every calendar operation — but the returned jsforce.Connection is built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` instead of the freshly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`. The new token is only written to the DB, so this request is pure overhead and the connection still relies on jsforce lazily refreshing the expired token again on 401. Also note this path always talks to Salesforce directly and never uses refreshOAuthTokens, so it ignores credential-sync mode entirely (and will break once the stored refresh_token is the placeholder written by parseRefreshTokenResponse).

findings.title: Sync-mode token response has no expires_in, so stored MS Teams token is immediately expired and loses its refresh token
findings.body: The documented contract for the sync endpoint is that it returns only the access token and expiry date, but this code computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + (responseBody?.expires_in || 0) * 1000` and persists `responseBody` as the credential key. In sync mode expires_in is absent, so expiry_date ≈ now and `isExpired` is true on every subsequent call (a refresh request to the sync endpoint on every operation), and the stored key no longer contains refresh_token at all, breaking any later non-sync refresh.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !==
findings.body: The endpoint authenticates by comparing the secret header to process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET with `!==`, a non-constant-time string comparison that leaks prefix matches through response timing. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual over equal-length buffers).

findings.title: findFirst-then-create allows duplicate credentials for the same user/app
findings.body: The lookup-then-insert sequence is not atomic and the Credential table has no unique constraint on (userId, appId). Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app both take the create branch and produce duplicate credentials; later reads that use findFirst may then pick up a stale credential. Use an upsert backed by a unique constraint or a transaction with appropriate isolation.

findings.title: Invalid payloads and decryption failures produce unhandled 500s
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throw on malformed bodies, bad ciphertext, or non-JSON plaintext, resulting in unhandled 500 errors (and there is no HTTP method restriction, so a plain GET also 500s). Use safeParse/try-catch and return 400 with a clear message.

findings.title: Updating an existing credential does not clear the invalid flag
findings.body: When a credential already exists only `key` is updated. Credentials previously flagged `invalid: true` (e.g. googlecalendar marks them on invalid_grant) stay invalid after fresh keys are synced in, so the integration remains disabled even though valid tokens were delivered. Set `invalid: false` when updating the key.
